title: Lunch Above the Traffic
summaryZh: Sofia 想把辦公室閒置屋頂改成午休花園，但承重、預算與維護問題讓完整計畫無法立即獲准，團隊只能在一週內做出可移動的示範區。

sentences.text: At noon, Sofia looked across the accounting office and counted eleven people eating at their desks.
sentences.zh: 中午時，Sofia 環顧會計辦公室，數到十一個人正在自己的座位上吃飯。

sentences.text: Some answered messages between bites, while others stared silently at the same screens they had watched all morning.
sentences.zh: 有些人邊吃邊回訊息，另一些人則沉默盯著已經看了一整個早上的螢幕。

sentences.text: The break room had only four chairs, and traffic noise filled the narrow sidewalk outside.
sentences.zh: 休息室只有四張椅子，外頭狹窄的人行道又充滿車流噪音。

sentences.text: Sofia remembered a roof door she had passed during a safety exercise the previous month.
sentences.zh: Sofia 想起上個月安全演練時曾經走過的一扇屋頂門。

sentences.text: Facilities manager Ravi unlocked it and led her up a short concrete staircase.
sentences.zh: 設施經理 Ravi 打開門，帶她走上一小段水泥樓梯。

sentences.text: Above them was an empty roof with old chairs, shipping boxes, and a wide view of the city.
sentences.zh: 上方是一處空蕩的屋頂，放著舊椅子和貨運紙箱，還能看見寬廣的城市景色。

sentences.text: Although the street remained busy below, the air on the roof felt cooler and surprisingly calm.
sentences.zh: 雖然下方街道仍然繁忙，屋頂上的空氣卻更涼爽，也出乎意料地平靜。

sentences.text: Sofia pictured tables, herbs, and coworkers returning downstairs after a genuine rest.
sentences.zh: Sofia 想像著桌子、香草植物，以及真正休息過後再回到樓下的同事。

sentences.text: She proposed turning one corner into a small garden where employees could eat lunch.
sentences.zh: 她提議把其中一個角落改成小花園，讓員工可以在那裡吃午餐。

sentences.text: Ravi liked the purpose behind the idea, but he warned that an attractive idea was not automatically a practical one.
sentences.zh: Ravi 喜歡這個構想背後的目的，但提醒她，吸引人的點子不一定自動就是可行的方案。

sentences.text: Heavy planters could exceed the roof's safe load, especially after wet soil absorbed rain.
sentences.zh: 沉重的花盆可能超過屋頂的安全承重，尤其是土壤吸收雨水之後。

sentences.text: Water could also block drains or leak through a surface that had never supported a garden.
sentences.zh: 水也可能堵住排水孔，或滲過從未承載過花園的屋頂表面。

sentences.text: Then there were wind, insurance, cleaning, and the question of who would care for everything.
sentences.zh: 此外還有強風、保險、清潔，以及究竟該由誰照顧一切的問題。

sentences.text: Instead of abandoning the idea, Sofia asked Ravi to help her list every condition for approval.
sentences.zh: Sofia 沒有放棄，而是請 Ravi 幫忙列出獲得批准所需的每一項條件。

sentences.text: Their coworker June surveyed the staff and found that thirty people would use the space weekly.
sentences.zh: 同事 June 調查員工後發現，每週會有三十人願意使用這個空間。

sentences.text: The three prepared a simple budget and requested a meeting with their department director.
sentences.zh: 三人準備了一份簡單預算，並向部門主管要求開會討論。

sentences.text: Director Chen listened carefully, then declined to approve permanent construction without an engineering review.
sentences.zh: Chen 主管仔細聽完後，表示沒有工程審查就不能批准永久施工。

sentences.text: That review would take months and cost more than Sofia's entire proposed garden.
sentences.zh: 那項審查會花上數月，而且費用比 Sofia 提議的整座花園還高。

sentences.text: However, the director offered them one week and a limited budget for a movable demonstration area.
sentences.zh: 不過，主管給他們一週時間和有限預算，製作一個可移動的示範區。

sentences.text: Nothing could be attached to the roof, and every object had to be carried away quickly.
sentences.zh: 任何物品都不能固定在屋頂上，而且每樣東西都必須能迅速搬走。

sentences.text: Sofia worried that such strict limits would make the demonstration look temporary and unconvincing.
sentences.zh: Sofia 擔心這些嚴格限制會讓示範區顯得臨時又缺乏說服力。

sentences.text: Ravi argued that the limits could guide them toward a safer design rather than a weaker one.
sentences.zh: Ravi 認為，這些限制能引導他們做出更安全的設計，而不是更差的設計。

sentences.text: June suggested starting with six seats, lightweight containers, and plants donated by employees.
sentences.zh: June 建議先準備六個座位、輕量容器，以及由員工捐出的植物。

sentences.text: By the meeting's end, disappointment had become a short list of tasks.
sentences.zh: 會議結束時，原本的失望已經變成一張簡短的工作清單。

sentences.text: Ravi measured the demonstration corner and marked a clear path to every drain and emergency exit.
sentences.zh: Ravi 測量示範區的角落，並標出通往每個排水孔和緊急出口的暢通路線。

sentences.text: June collected folding chairs, mint plants, and shallow wooden boxes from willing coworkers.
sentences.zh: June 從願意幫忙的同事那裡收集折疊椅、薄荷盆栽和淺木箱。

sentences.text: Sofia created a watering schedule and persuaded the cafeteria to lend them two small tables.
sentences.zh: Sofia 製作澆水輪值表，並說服員工餐廳借給他們兩張小桌子。

sentences.text: On Friday afternoon, the empty corner became a modest place to sit, talk, and breathe with a view of downtown.
sentences.zh: 星期五下午，空蕩的角落變成一處可以坐下、交談、喘口氣並眺望市中心的樸素空間。

sentences.text: Nothing was permanent, yet each piece could be moved by one person in less than a minute.
sentences.zh: 沒有任何東西是永久設置的，但每件物品都能由一個人在一分鐘內搬動。

sentences.text: The team took photographs and planned to invite Director Chen for lunch on Monday.
sentences.zh: 團隊拍下照片，打算星期一邀請 Chen 主管上來吃午餐。

sentences.text: Before leaving on Friday, Ravi's weather application warned of unusually strong winds over the weekend.
sentences.zh: 星期五離開前，Ravi 的天氣應用程式警告，週末將出現異常強風。

sentences.text: Nobody was scheduled to visit the roof over the weekend, so their gentle idea would face the strong winds alone.
sentences.zh: 週末沒有人預定前往屋頂，因此他們溫和的構想將獨自面對強風。

questions.q: Why did Sofia want to create a rooftop lunch area?
options: Coworkers had few comfortable places to take a real break
The company needed more space for accounting records
The cafeteria planned to close for several months

questions.q: Which concern did Ravi raise about heavy planters?
options: They might block the view from nearby offices
They could exceed the roof's safe load when wet
They would attract too many employees at lunch
A permanent garden with an unlimited budget
An immediate engineering review of the whole building
A movable demonstration area with one week to prepare it
